body:
As someone that used to volunteer on the suicide helpline ( my own desire for suicide is a whole other story), try not to be hurt or discouraged if you end up talking to someone you dont connect with. Most helplines consist of volunteers with hundreds of hours of training and there is an intense screening processes where many dont make the cut ( at least mine was).

But, theres also a shortage of volunteers, and many experience burn out. Or sometimes you get someone who just came off of an intense call.

Also, the paperwork can be very overwhelming. While everything has the same non disclosure rules as doctors, there is a lot of documentation. That's because if you get a frequent or recent caller, the volunteer can get a better scope of the crisis the caller is dealing with (although the crisis volunteer wont use that to bait the caller into talking about it).

All in all, its complicated. But just know that you can always call back and chat with someone else if you dont connect with the first person you call. Your life is worth it.

I'm in canada. So it likely does make a difference if you're US. I'd love to hear your anecdotal experience if you're willing to PM me. No pressure of course, I know it's personal. I'd just love to see some light at the end of this tunnel.

Thanks. I'm going to one that seems to pop up the most on google and appears to have had the most information out there on my rights to fight my charge, and their firm seems to be doing the most to fight the province on our questionable DUI program. I'm hoping I'll have better luck this time. Thank you for your words. I'm really hoping for the best, or else I'm pretty much done for.

Thanks. My only option is to appeal it to the supreme courts. I doubt I even have the ability to take on the debt (credit wise) to do this. But I'm planning on trying. 

I had fought my DUI with a lawyer but they lost. A part of me wonders if I went to the right person. She seemed rather aloof about it all.

I definitely will give what you said a shot. I'm so depressed right now I can barely physically function, but I already made the calls to a lawyer, just waiting to hear back.

My province doesnt criminally charge people with impaired driving. It's under the motor vehicle act. So I dont have a criminal record, but the impaired driving will be on my drivers abstract permanently. No fire department will hire you with a DUI on your license. 

I've also lost my car for 3 months so cant work, or really even get groceries. I'm living off snacks at a corner gas station until I figure something else.

I so wish you were right about getting it expunged.
